opex.note: Developing new vehicles, battery cells and AI for self-driving.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative

footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $1,144M; $1,129M of it was attributable to common stockholders and $15M to noncontrolling interests and redeemable noncontrolling interests in subsidiaries. Figures are from Tesla's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2024 (filed April 24, 2024), cross-checked to the Q1 2024 update letter filed as Exhibit 99.1 to the Form 8-K on April 23, 2024; deliveries, production and energy storage deployments are from the production and deliveries release filed as Exhibit 99.1 to the Form 8-K on April 2, 2024. No rounding adjustment was needed: the filings already report in whole millions and all totals balance exactly.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue fell to $21,301M from $23,329M in Q1 2023, mainly on lower vehicle prices and fewer deliveries.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: Diluted earnings per share attributable to common stockholders, down from $0.73 in Q1 2023.

kpis.label: Deliveries
kpis.note: Down 9% from 422,875 a year earlier; production was 433,371, hit by the updated Model 3 ramp in Fremont and disruptions at Gigafactory Berlin.

kpis.label: Energy storage deployed
kpis.note: A record quarter — described in the release as the highest deployment yet — up 4% from 3,889 MWh in Q1 2023.

otherDetail: Net $382M of other income: $350M of interest income on cash and short-term investments, plus $108M of other income (mainly foreign-exchange gains on intercompany balances), minus $76M of interest expense.

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Cars: $16,460M of vehicle sales, plus $442M of regulatory credits and $476M of leasing.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack and Powerwall batteries and solar; higher Megapack prices offset fewer solar deployments.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Repairs and maintenance, Supercharging, insurance, parts sales and used cars.

takeaways.text: Operating income fell to $1,171M from $2,664M a year earlier. Lower average selling prices, fewer deliveries and the Cybertruck ramp outweighed cheaper raw materials, and overall gross margin narrowed to 17.4% from 19.3%.
takeaways.title: Car price cuts crushed operating profit

takeaways.text: Energy generation and storage gross profit jumped to $403M from $168M, lifting its gross margin to 24.6% from 11.0%, helped by Megapack and IRA manufacturing credits — on record storage deployments of 4,053 MWh.
takeaways.title: Energy became a real profit engine

takeaways.text: Research and development rose to $1,151M from $771M on AI, battery-cell and other new programs, and selling, general and administrative costs rose 28% to $1,374M, so total operating expenses climbed 37% even as revenue fell 9%.
takeaways.title: Spending on the future jumped while sales fell

verdict: Price cuts and a disrupted, lower-delivery quarter squeezed car profits sharply, even as energy storage hit a record and grew much more profitable.
